reuse.why: Adds a new getRangedAmount used by the existing getScheduledAmount, but the five server/shared sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The range rule itself is defined once, but the `== null ? 0 : number ? value : range` dispatch stays copied at four sites (and a number-or-range dispatch at the fifth) alongside the helper that already covers it.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Only the range rule, its call sites, comments, tests and a release note in the repo's usual format.

maintainability.why: A future change to the range rule is one edit, but having getRangedAmount and getScheduledAmount side by side with sites picking between them leaves the null/number handling scattered.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts keep their own dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining per-site dispatch is the pre-existing open copy, not reshaped; the range arithmetic itself is now shared.

one_place.where: getRangedAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, used by getScheduledAmount (client) and by all five server/shared sites that previously computed the midpoint.
